_provenance.method: build one Headers per guard (none / request / request-no-cors / response), set(name, value) on each, then get(name): null means the guard DROPPED it
_provenance.control: x-custom answers SET under guard `none`; if it ever reads DROP the probe is broken, not the browser
_provenance.why_not_the_spec: AUTONOMOUS-GOAL.md R3 and the project rule that webref is wrong in BOTH directions. The candidate NAMES below are only what was asked; every ANSWER is the browser's.
_provenance.limits: one browser, one build, one origin. A name absent here was not probed -- it is not a measurement that the name is allowed.

_provenance_widened.measured_from: Google Chrome 150.0.7871.46, --headless=new --dump-dom, http://127.0.0.1 -- the SAME build as above
_provenance_widened.by: CONF GUARD1, before writing the engine half
_provenance_widened.why: the name table alone could not answer four questions the implementation had to decide, and R3 forbids answering them from the spec. Each one is now the browser's answer, with a control beside it. The CASES section of the probe page is the script.
_provenance_widened.limits: same single browser/build/origin. Case H (is the NAME rule applied to `delete` too?) could NOT be measured: a forbidden name can never enter a guarded list in the first place, so no public API observes it. The engine applies the same rule to `delete` for one-implementation reasons, not because this file says so.

_user_agent_evidence: Chrome 150.0.7871.46, 2026-09-25 (REALWEB T6): `new Request(u, {headers: {'User-Agent': 'x'}}).headers` has no user-agent, and fetch(crossOrigin, {headers: {'User-Agent': 'page-ua'}}) goes out as a SIMPLE GET carrying the browser's own user-agent. Fetch removed User-Agent from the forbidden list; Chromium still drops it (crbug 571722). A bare `new Headers({'User-Agent': 'x'})` (guard none) keeps it in both.
_prefix_evidence: `proxy-foo` and `sec-foo` are not real header names and both DROP, so the rule is a PREFIX rule and not a fixed list. `sec-fetch-mode` drops for the same reason.
_safelist_evidence: under guard `request-no-cors` exactly these four survive; `range` is SET under `request` and DROP under `request-no-cors`, so it is NOT safelisted in this build.
_response_evidence: only these two drop under guard `response`. Note the asymmetry a copied list gets wrong: `set-cookie` is forbidden as a REQUEST header too, `set-cookie2` is not (it is SET under `request`).

readings.content-type: application/json: DROP -- so the NAME being safelisted is not enough
readings.accept: 'a' x 200: DROP -- a value longer than 128 bytes

_value_aware_evidence.consequence: the request-no-cors guard must ask the same question the wire path already asked, which in this engine is `modules/fetch/fetch_global.rs::no_cors_safelisted` -- promoted to pub(crate) rather than copied.

guard_of_a_new_header_list._method: probe CASES sections C, D, E, G, I -- construct the list, then set(name, value) and read it back
guard_of_a_new_header_list.new Headers(anotherHeaders): none -- a COPY of a guarded list is unguarded (case I3: the copy of a Request's headers takes `cookie`)
guard_of_a_new_header_list.new Request(url, {mode: 'no-cors'}).head: request-no-cors
guard_of_a_new_header_list.new Request(otherRequest).headers: the mode it INHERITS decides (case E: a Request built from a no-cors Request drops `range` and keeps `accept`)
guard_of_a_new_header_list.requestOrResponse.clone().headers: the original's guard, carried (case D, all three)
guard_of_a_new_header_list.Response.json(...).headers: response -- drops set-cookie, keeps x-custom (case G3/G4)
guard_of_a_new_header_list.Response.redirect(url).headers: immutable -- THROWS (case G1), while `location` reads back (case G2)

_init_evidence: case C: `new Request('/x', {headers: {cookie: 'x', 'x-custom': '1'}}).headers.get('cookie')` is null while `x-custom` is '1'. The guard is not only a check on LATER mutations -- the list is filled through it, so a forbidden name never enters.
_body_content_type_evidence: case B: `new Request(u, {mode: 'no-cors', method: 'POST', body: new Blob(['x'], {type: 'application/json'})}).headers.get('content-type')` is null; the CONTROL, the same request in `cors` mode, answers `application/json`, and a string body (text/plain;charset=UTF-8) survives under no-cors. So the Content-Type the body extraction adds goes through the guard like any other append -- an engine that stamps the guard AFTER that append keeps it and is wrong.

_combined_value_evidence.rule: under request-no-cors, `append(name, value)` is judged against what `get(name)` WOULD answer afterwards -- the values already present for that name, then value, joined with ', '. `set` is NOT, because `set` replaces.

controls.append x-custom twice under no-cors: null -- a non-safelisted name never gets the chance to combine

_combined_value_evidence.consequence: a guard applied to a list that is already full must REPLAY the fill rather than filter entry by entry, because each entry's verdict depends on the ones kept before it.

_no_op_evidence: every DROP above was a `get` answering null with nothing thrown. Only `immutable` throws, and its words are `Failed to execute '<member>' on 'Headers': Headers are immutable`.
